correctness.rationale: The finite connected multipartite graph has diameter <=2. Packing forces every color >=2 to be a singleton, and any color-one vertices to lie within one independent part. Every high-color singleton broadcasts globally. A block containing only color-one vertices can dominate precisely when it is the entire color-one class and that class equals a full part. This proves kappa=h+1 exactly for full parts and kappa=h otherwise, including absence of color 1. Counting vertex subsets and injective assignments gives E. For W, partition h distinct high-color vertices into k unordered nonempty blocks (Stirling S(h,k)), attach s color-one vertices independently (k^s); in the whole-part case there is exactly one further option: a separate color-one block and S(h,k-1). The lower palette bound max(n-a+1,k) and forced equality cases yield the displayed k-spectrum/optimizer multiplicities, with k=n and complete-graph boundaries checked. Independently recomputed five profiles (K_3, K_{2,2}, K_{3,1}, K_{2,1,1}, K_{3,2}) at six palette values each by full graph-distance packing and set-partition enumeration, matching E and W exactly. The unrestricted proof is structural; finite tests only corroborate.
